result.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
result.summary: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 in-context 视觉世界模型：用对比损失把角色其他动作片段编码为「body code」，以区分外观相同但动力学不同的角色，并构建含 144 个 2D 卡通角色的 ToonTwins 基准，报告 twins 识别率 85.9% 及路径预测误差约 8.5% 的改善。
AI.relevance_reason: 把上下文片段压缩成任务相关的「body code」并用对比损失保证区分性，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态的可分性监督提供线索；而其 latent 像素世界模型仅恢复不足 25% 的跳跃高度差，可供核查 latent 内容是否真正被下游使用（信息坍缩）这一常见诊断问题。
